title: The Case for Reading Slowly
summaryZh: 作者反省把閱讀變成數量競賽的風氣，主張慢讀才可能真正改變一個人的想法。

sentences.text: Somewhere along the way, reading turned into a numbers game, and I think we lost something real.
sentences.zh: 不知道從什麼時候開始，閱讀變成了一場數字競賽，我覺得我們因此失去了某些真實的東西。
sentences.note: turned into 的 d 連到 into 的母音；lost something 的 t 被後面的 s 吃掉。

sentences.text: People post their yearly totals the way runners post mileage, as though books were distance covered.
sentences.zh: 大家貼出年度讀書總量，就像跑者貼里程數，好像書本只是跑過的距離。

sentences.text: I did it too for about three years, and I can barely tell you what was in any of them.
sentences.zh: 我也這樣做了大概三年，而我幾乎說不出裡面任何一本寫了什麼。
sentences.note: did it 的 d 在母音間變閃音，連成 /ˈdɪ.ɾɪt/；can 弱讀成 /kən/。

sentences.text: What I remember instead are the four or five books I read badly, slowly, over and over.
sentences.zh: 我真正記得的，反而是那四五本我讀得笨拙、緩慢、一遍又一遍的書。

sentences.text: I underlined things, argued in the margins, and put the book down for a week when I got stuck.
sentences.zh: 我畫線、在頁邊跟作者爭辯，卡住的時候就把書放下一個禮拜。
sentences.note: put the book down 的 t 變喉塞音；got stuck 的 t 完全不釋放。

sentences.text: That's not efficient by any measure, and it would look pretty terrible on one of those reading challenges.
sentences.zh: 不管用什麼標準看那都不算有效率，放到那種閱讀挑戰上還挺難看的。

sentences.text: But those are the only books that have actually changed the way I think about anything at all.
sentences.zh: 但那些書，才是真正改變了我對任何事情看法的書。

sentences.text: The argument for speed is that there is simply too much worth reading to linger anywhere.
sentences.zh: 支持速讀的說法是：值得讀的東西太多了，根本沒有停留的餘裕。

sentences.text: I get that anxiety completely, though I'd argue that it gets the whole problem exactly backwards.
sentences.zh: 那種焦慮我完全懂，但我認為它把整個問題想反了。
sentences.note: though 在句中是轉折信號，語調先下降再略微提起，提示後面要推翻前半句。

sentences.text: If almost nothing sticks, then reading fifty books a year is closer to fifty near misses.
sentences.zh: 如果幾乎什麼都留不下來，那一年讀五十本比較像是五十次擦身而過。

sentences.text: Slowness is not a virtue on its own, and I'm not romanticizing the dusty armchair here.
sentences.zh: 慢本身不是美德，我也不是在美化那種佈滿灰塵的扶手椅畫面。

sentences.text: It just happens to be the speed at which an argument can push back against what you believe.
sentences.zh: 慢只是剛好是一個論點能夠反過來衝撞你既有信念的速度。
sentences.note: happens to be 的 to 弱讀成 /tə/；at which 連讀，at 的 t 變閃音。

sentences.text: You can't really be persuaded by a book you're skimming, because skimming mostly confirms what you already brought to it.
sentences.zh: 你不可能被一本你只是快速掃過的書說服，因為掃讀多半只會印證你原本帶進去的東西。

sentences.text: So I've stopped counting, and the strange result is that I now finish fewer books and keep more.
sentences.zh: 所以我不再計數了，奇怪的結果是我現在讀完的書更少，留下來的卻更多。
sentences.note: fewer 和 more 是一組對比重音，兩個字都要明顯加重，句意全靠這組對比成立。

sentences.text: Whatever reading is for, I'm fairly sure it isn't for the number at the end of December.
sentences.zh: 不管閱讀是為了什麼，我相當確定它不是為了十二月底的那個數字。

questions.q: What does the writer say about the years he spent counting books?
options: He remembers almost nothing from them
He read mostly fiction during that time
He enjoyed reading more then than he does now

questions.q: What is the writer's attitude toward slow reading?
options: He treats slowness as a virtue in its own right
He values it because it gives an argument time to change your mind
He thinks it only suits difficult academic books

questions.q: Why does he say skimming cannot persuade you?
options: It is too tiring to keep up
You mostly pick up what you already believed
Most books are not worth arguing with
